clips.title: TDD, AI agents and coding with Kent Beck
clips.why: Kent Beck, who created test-driven development, explains why he still writes tests first with AI agents, and what his "genie" does to tests when it is stuck.
look: Tests are how he tells the genie what "correct" means, so a test that changes under him is a lost requirement.
Listen for what an agent does when a test stands between it and "done". That is a false heal, in his words.
clips.after: Our CI fixer has the same temptation every time main is red, which is why its diff is read by a check it cannot argue with.

clips.title: Stop Letting Claude Code Grade Its Own Work
clips.why: A small experiment: an agent says PASS on a broken feature, its own verify step agrees, and a check written as a skill gets skipped. It is the argument for putting checks in code.
look: The agent's own verdict and the hidden tests disagree. Whose word should a pipeline trust?
The difference between a skill, which the agent may skip, and a hook, which always runs.
clips.after: The false-heal check runs from the Stop hook and again before any PR, so it never depends on the agent choosing to run it.

practice.q: Which of these changes is NOT a false heal?

options.why: The expectation was changed to match the broken output. The never-rule edit_test_assertions rejects it.

options.text: projectCount < 0 ? "No projects yet" : ""  becomes  projectCount === 0 ? "No projects yet" : ""
options.why: This changes the code and leaves the test alone. It is the honest fix.
More retries let a failing test pass by luck. For retries, a higher number is looser.

practice.q: Finish the rule for thresholds: for fail-under a lower value is looser, and for retries and timeouts a value that goes ___ is looser.
practice.before: retries and timeouts are loosened when the new value goes
practice.hint: More retries and longer timeouts let more failures through.
practice.why: A test that may retry or wait longer can pass while the behaviour is still wrong.

practice.q: A CI fixer adds test.only( to the one test it fixed. CI is green. What does the check say?

options.text: Nothing: .only makes a test run, it does not skip it
options.why: .only runs that one test and silently skips every other test in the file. That is a weakened suite.

options.text: A new skip, because .only skips every other test
options.why: The SKIP pattern includes .only for exactly this reason.
No assertion line changed. The finding is the new .only.

practice.q: Put the CI fixer's steps in order, from claiming the VM to a PR.
items: Run the failed commands at main's head in the VM: is it us?
Red in the VM, so make the smallest fix inside the charter's paths
Say done; the Stop hook runs the false-heal check and sends the agent back if it finds anything
Before any PR, the false-heal check runs again on the final diff
The scope judge reads the diff with the charter, and only then is a PR opened
practice.why: Reproduce first, fix second, and check twice: once where the agent can still repair it, and once as the wall.

practice.q: Nova's PR and a routine's run both contain a new it.skip. What is different?

options.why: Nova's work was asked for by a person, so the finding is shown to the reviewer instead.

options.text: Nova's PR shows a flag for the reviewer; the routine's run is rejected as false_heal and opens no PR
options.why: Routines act without a requester asking, so any finding rejects the run and moves the routine down the ladder.

options.text: The routine's PR shows a flag; Nova's run is rejected
options.why: It is the other way round. Routines get the strict rule.
